solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Contracted loyal worker? Not this one

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the word for loyal loses its final letter

parts.note: a loyal friend is a true one
the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

explanation.surface: A question about a contracted employee who stays faithful, then a denial that this one qualifies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' trims TRUE to TRU. The definition leans on the whole clue: a pupil who skips school is precisely not a loyal worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil playing hooky is the opposite of a dutiful attender, the one who is not loyal to lessons.

clue.text: Dances with superior meals, where one can buy drinks

indicators.note: in a down clue superior means placed above, so the meals word sits on top of the dances word

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: An evening of dancing paired with a better class of food at a place serving drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'tea' can be an evening meal, so TEAS are meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Cafes serving tea and cakes are places where a customer can order a cuppa.

clue.text: I buy extravagant clothing to renounce commonness

indicators.note: clothing means dressing round, so the scrambled letters wrap the word for renounce
extravagant means wild or excessive, signalling that the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to quit something is to give it up or renounce it

explanation.surface: A shopper vows to give up showy spending on clothes in order to stop being so ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like garments but is the container signal; 'extravagant' mixes the shopper's own words rather than describing spending.
explanation.definitionFit: Being found everywhere is a kind of commonness; the word means omnipresence.

clue.text: Niche device for the bookworm

definitions.meaning: a recess or small corner set into a wall or room
an e-reader sold by Barnes and Noble, for those who read a lot

explanation.surface: A reading gadget aimed at a specialist market of book lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A small recess is a corner, and the same word is the brand of an electronic book reader.

clue.text: Pole knocked out another in quiz, ultimately ambitious gentlemen

indicators.note: knocked out means one letter ousts another, the first pole replacing the second

parts.note: to quiz someone is to enquire of them

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of ambitious

parts.note: N is the other pole, north
S is the south pole

explanation.surface: A Polish contestant in a quiz eliminates a rival, and the eventual winners are ambitious gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: ENQUIRE plus S (last of ambitious) gives ENQUIRES; 'knocked out' has the S pole replace the N pole. 'Pole' looks like a nationality but is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The courtesy title written after a man's name marks him as a gentleman, so the plural covers gentlemen.

clue.text: Post above establishment signifying traditional trade

indicators.note: in a down clue above puts the first word over the second

parts.note: to ship goods is to send or post them
an establishment can be a building, as in a business premises

explanation.surface: A position held over a firm, said to stand for a long-standing craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a job, but it is the verb to send.
explanation.definitionFit: Constructing vessels is a long-established industry, the kind of heavy craft in old port towns.

clue.text: Herbivore raised on grass, fuel vaguely disagreeable

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first piece above the next
raised in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the gnu, or wildebeest, is a grazing antelope
grass and rat both mean an informer

indicators.note: vaguely signals the letters of the following word are muddled

explanation.surface: A grazing animal reared on grass, its fuel needs vaguely unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns GNU into UNG; 'vaguely' muddles FUEL into EFUL. 'grass' is not pasture but the slang for an informer, RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no thanks is churlish behaviour, so the word can stand for unpleasant or disagreeable.

clue.text: Lift in order fills constantly, going up

indicators.note: fills means goes inside, so the word for in order is placed within the other
going up in a down clue means the word is reversed

parts.note: ever means always or constantly
OK means all right or in order

explanation.surface: An elevator in working order keeps filling up as it rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' tempts as an elevator, but it is the verb to lift a ban; 'going up' reverses the word for constantly, and 'fills' puts the in-order word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift a ban or restriction is to cancel or rescind it.

clue.text: Recognise learner interrupting cook

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the learner letter goes inside the cooking word

parts.note: to saute is to fry quickly
L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: An apprentice breaks into the chef's work and is duly acknowledged.
explanation.definitionFit: Saluting someone acknowledges them, as in honouring achievement.

clue.text: Author's travel document rejected when entering Missouri

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the state abbreviation sits within the reversed document
rejected means turned back, so the document's word is reversed

parts.note: a visa is an entry permit stamped in a passport
MO is the US postal abbreviation for Missouri

explanation.surface: A writer's visa is refused when he tries to enter Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses the document's word, and 'entering' puts the state's postal code inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific science-fiction writer, author of I, Robot.

clue.text: Giving criminal, missing outside, ball of gum

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order
missing outside means the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A criminal handing over a ball of chewing gum, with nobody outside to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges the first word, and 'missing outside' trims ball to its middle pair. 'gum' is not chewing gum but the flesh round the teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is the dental term for things relating to the gums.

clue.text: Doctor, Frenchman's negative about his cash flow

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the French negative wraps the rest

parts.note: non is French for no
the Frenchman's money is the euro
a surge is a sudden flow or rush

explanation.surface: A French doctor says no to his money troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers back to the Frenchman, so his cash is the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain surgeon is a medical specialist, a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Reportedly, where one might find students to pull

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is the one that sounds alike

parts.note: a hall of residence houses university students

explanation.surface: Rumour has it you can tug students out of somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a hall (of residence) is student housing at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag something heavy is to pull it along.

clue.text: Killjoy melting snow could be described as such

definitions.meaning: a spoilsport who dampens everyone's fun

definitions.text: melting snow could be described as such
definitions.meaning: thawing snow is literally a soggy white cover lying on the ground

explanation.surface: A grumpy person describing a thaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport is idiomatically a damp cover thrown over fun; literally, slush is a soaked covering.

clue.text: Axes cut, that man's in possession of functioning instruments

parts.note: x and y are the axes of a graph
to lop is to cut off

indicators.note: in possession of means holding, so the first word wraps the functioning word

parts.note: he's is that man is, written without the apostrophe
on means working or functioning

explanation.surface: A man wielding axes, chopping away, while holding working instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like chopping tools but means the x and y axes of a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: These are percussion instruments with wooden bars struck by mallets.

clue.text: Knowing where to go for trade-in?

parts.note: the letters of trade-in are those of trained made crazy, potty being slang for mad

explanation.surface: A question about being sure which shop to visit for a part-exchange deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: TRAINED gone 'potty' (crazy) gives the anagram TRADE-IN, so the clue's last word is the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler who has learned toilet habits knows where to go when nature calls.

clue.text: Quite inclined to bathe with one's husband

parts.note: to steep something is to soak or bathe it
one is I, so one's is I'S, read as I plus S

explanation.surface: Someone rather keen to take a bath together with her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclined' looks like willing but means sloping.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope fairly sharp in gradient is rather steep, the suffix softening it.

clue.text: View university catalogue American's left

indicators.note: left means departed, so the American letters go missing

parts.note: a prospectus is a university's guide to its courses
US for American

explanation.surface: Someone looks over a university brochure an American has left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like abandoned but means the US letters have gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a wide scene or vista, such as a panorama.

clue.text: One investigating settlement's ground uses old jars to contain sediment, ultimately

indicators.note: to contain means to hold inside, so the scrambled letters enclose the final letter
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the last letter of sediment

explanation.surface: An archaeologist digging at a settlement uses old jars to hold sediment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' scrambles USES OLD JARS, and 'to contain' holds the T from sediment within. 'settlement' is not a village but an insurance payout.
explanation.definitionFit: This insurance assessor investigates claims to decide what payout should be made.

clue.text: Banks in Odense set up with investment of sweep's money

indicators.note: investment means putting inside, so the sweeping word goes within
set up in a down clue means the letters are reversed
banks are the edges, so the outer letters of the town are taken

parts.note: to scud is to sweep or skim along swiftly

explanation.surface: Banks in a Danish city set up a chimney sweep's investment fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks in' takes O and E from Odense; 'set up' reverses them to EO, and SCUD goes inside after E.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the former currency of Portugal and still is in Cape Verde.

clue.text: Push on to cook lavish meal

indicators.note: to cook means to fiddle or tamper, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Pressing on with preparing a lavish dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a large, slap-up meal or feast, from nosh meaning food.

clue.text: Talk about parent being overprotective

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the talk word goes round the parent

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing or talking to police
a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: A discussion of a parent who coddles too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk' means to sing, informer's slang; it wraps MOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Stifling care that leaves a child no room is overbearing affection.

clue.text: Comically dozes, emitting those heartily

indicators.note: comically means in a jokey way, signalling the letters are mixed
emitting means giving out, so a letter is removed from the scrambled word
heartily points to the centre letter of those

explanation.surface: Someone nods off in comic fashion, snoring loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comically' scrambles DOZES; 'emitting' drops O, the heart of 'those'. The whole clue also defines: comic strips show sleep as a string of Z's.
explanation.definitionFit: In cartoons a sleeping figure gives off a stream of the last letter, signifying snoring.

clue.text: Fair lot to talk about

indicators.note: to talk about means as spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: one's lot in life is one's fate

explanation.surface: A funfair giving people plenty to chat about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' is the noun, a village gala, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A village gala or bazaar is an outdoor fair with stalls.

clue.text: Let go of worker ensnared by a French journalist

parts.note: un is French for a
a hand is a manual worker
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A French reporter traps a worker and then lets go.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhand someone is to release one's grip on them, a rather old-fashioned phrase.

clue.text: European city playing against European city

parts.note: v for versus, as in team fixtures
Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: One European city's team taking on another's in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian lagoon city of canals and gondolas is a famous tourist destination.

clue.text: Showing off on piano after old rival

indicators.note: after means the later pieces come behind the old letter
on in an across clue means following, so showing off comes after piano

parts.note: p is the musical marking for soft, piano
posing means showing off

explanation.surface: Someone shows off at the piano after an old rival appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rival' is the adjective, as in opposing camps.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing sides are competing ones, so the word fits as an adjective for rival.

clue.text: Scarlet — victim of revolver? Eliminated lead piping

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red

indicators.note: eliminated lead means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a gunshot victim is said to be shot

explanation.surface: A colour, a gunshot victim, and a killing involving lead pipe, like a murder mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead piping' suggests the murder weapon, but 'lead' is a first letter and 'piping' (as in piping hot) the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Food served piping is extremely hot, so the phrase for glowing with heat fits.
